entry.title: MouseEvent.movementX/Y - update events that set a value
entry.content:
MouseEvent.movementX and MouseEvent.movementY state that the value is only set for mousemove event. In fact it is also set for pointermove on Chrome and FF, and pointerrawupdate on Chrome and FF from version 148.

This adds the clarification.

entry.title: Issue assignment process clarification
entry.content:
The Guidelines for working on an issue suggest that users self assign if they can, and otherwise add a comment asking to be assigned.

In theory this is good - user asks to be assigned, and a core user then assigns them. Historically though this often doesn't work - you get people asking to be assigned to multiple issues, then getting assigned and doing no work. The issues then rot.

The current and well established process is that authors start work and create the cross link Fixes #<issue no.> in the PR to implicitly assign the issue.

  • The weakness in the process is that there is a window where multiple users might attempt to take the issue, and it is a little harder to see who owns the issue.
  • The benefit is that it is clear that the assignee is actually working on the issue, and you can still assign as needed etc.

This updates the process to reflect how assignment is actually handled on MDN.

entry.title: docs: Add examples and migration guides to deprecated HTML elements and Web Audio APIs
entry.content:
Overview

This PR improves documentation completeness by adding self-contained examples and migration guides to deprecated HTML elements and Web Audio API interfaces that previously only referred to factory methods or other pages.

Changes Made

Deprecated HTML Elements

  • <font> element - Added comprehensive Examples section and Migration Guide

    • Shows deprecated usage patterns alongside modern CSS alternatives
    • Includes migration table mapping color, face, and size attributes to CSS properties
    • Demonstrates best practices using external stylesheets

  • <frame> element - Enhanced with modern <iframe> alternatives

    • Provides side-by-side comparison with complete, runnable code
    • Includes responsive CSS Grid layout example
    • Added Migration Guide explaining accessibility and performance improvements

Web Audio API Improvements

  • ChannelSplitterNode - Replaced single factory method reference with 3 practical examples

    • Basic channel splitting for stereo audio
    • Analyzing individual channels with analysers
    • Handling multi-channel sources (6+ channels)

  • DelayNode - Replaced single factory method reference with 4 practical examples

    • Simple delay effect setup
    • Feedback delay effect (echo) with dry/wet mixing
    • Automating delay time with ramp functions
    • Breaking feedback loops (explaining why DelayNode is essential)

Impact

  • Better developer experience: Developers no longer need to navigate to factory methods to find examples
  • Clearer migration paths: Deprecated elements now show explicit before/after code comparisons
  • Improved learning: Web Audio API pages are now self-contained with practical, real-world examples
  • Enhanced accessibility: Migration guides help developers understand why changes are needed

Statistics

  • Files modified: 9
  • Lines added: 365+
  • Code examples added: 11
  • Comprehensive migration guides: 2

Testing

  • Verified all code examples are syntactically correct
  • Cross-checked references between related documentation pages
  • Confirmed migration guides are technically accurate
  • Examples follow MDN code style guidelines
